verdict.left_looks: A two-storey-looking Japanese-style house on a stone-and-mossy-grass plinth with a dark stepped roof of grey/black stone-brick tiles, upturned eave tips and a small chimney. Walls are dark wood planks with lighter wood trim and a horizontal band of plank cladding, paper-like window panels and lanterns flanking the entrance. The stairs are stone-brick with a wooden landing. Patchy moss, mixed grey stone and mossy grass in the base read as deliberate weathering. Views show a clear porch-like front and a fuller, more enclosed volume from the side.
verdict.right_looks: A dark open pavilion on a grey stone-brick base: a tiered, stepped hip roof of dark wood-brick with wide overhangs, a raised timber platform with railings and lantern posts, and a recessed colonnade of dark square-ish pillars with a few small windows. Entrance is a single stone step. The roof reads as a stepped pyramid from every side, the body is mostly open or railed, and the whole thing is very uniform in dark brown with little contrast. Lanterns and the grey plinth give it some punctuation.
verdict.why: The left build has a legible enclosed house form, varied materials (stone, moss, grass, wood, paper windows) and a clear entrance, while the right is a dark, monotone open pavilion whose stepped roof dominates and whose body reads as a colonnade rather than a building.
